title: Recording, mixing: Daytime Nighttime Suffering by Wings | 1979
content:
Replica Studio, London
Producers: Paul McCartney, Chris Thomas

Wings finished recording the ‘Goodnight Tonight’ single b-side ‘Daytime Nighttime Suffering’ on 16 January 1979.

The basic track had been recorded the previous day.

During this session Paul McCartney overdubbed his lead vocals and an autoharp part. He then added triple-tracked harmony vocals, joined by Linda McCartney and Denny Laine.

There was also a cameo appearance by young James McCartney.

At one point the elevator opened, and Linda came out with baby James in her arms, and he actually went, ‘aaaah.’ And that’s on the recording—you can hear it if you listen carefully, it’s right over one of the stops where there’s a little drum break.
Steve Holley, 1 July 2020
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 2: 1974-80

A rough stereo mix was made towards the end of the session, and taken away by Paul.
